44.19: Abraham was the greet fadir of the multitude of folkis; and noon was foundun lijk hym in glorie, which kepte the lawe of hiy God, and was in the testament with hym.
44.20: He made a testament to stonde in his fleisch; and he was foundun feithful in temptacioun.
44.21: Therfor God with an ooth yaf to hym glorie in his folk; God made hym to encreesse, as an heep of erthe, and to enhaunse his seed as sterris, and to enherite hem fro the see `til to the see, and fro the flood `til to the endis of erthe. And to Isaac God dide in the same maner, for Abraham, his fadir.
44.22: The Lord yaf to hym the blessing of alle folkis; and confermyde his testament on the heed of Jacob.
44.23: He knew hym in hise blessyngis, and yaf eritage to hym; and departide to hym a part in twelue lynagis. And he kepte to hym men of merci, fyndynge grace in the siyt of eche man.

45.1: Moises was loued of God and of men; whose mynde is in blessyng.
45.2: He made him lijk in the glorie of seyntis, and he magnefiede hym in the drede of enemyes; and in his wordis he made peesible the wondris ayens kynde.
45.3: He glorifiede hym in the siyt of kyngis, and he `comaundide to hym bifore his puple, and schewide his glorie to hym.
45.4: In the feith and myldenesse of hym God made hym hooli; and chees him of alle men.
45.5: For he herde hym, and his vois; and ledde in hym in a cloude. And yaf to hym an herte to comaundementis, and to the lawe of lijf, and of techyng; to teche Jacob a testament, and Israel hise domes.
45.6: He made hiy Aaron, his brother, and lijk hym of the lynage of Leuy.
45.7: He ordeynede to hym euerlastynge testament, and yaf to hym the preesthod of the folk. And he made hym blissful in glorie,
45.8: and girte hym with a girdil of riytfulnesse; and clothide hym with a stoole of glorie, and crownede hym in the ournementis of vertu.
45.9: He settide on hym sandalies, and breeches, and a clooth on the schuldur, and girte hym aboute with ful many small goldun bellis in cumpas; to yyue soun in his goyng, to make soun herd in the temple, in to mynde to the sones of his folk.
45.10: God yaf to hym an hooli stoole, a wouun werk, with gold, and iacynct, and purpur, the werk of a wijs man, maad riche with doom and treuthe;
45.11: the werk of a crafti man, in writhun reed threed, with preciouse iemmes grauun in the byndyng of gold, and grauun bi the werk of a crafti man of stoonys, in to mynde, bi the noumbre of the lynagis of Israel.
45.12: A goldun coroun on his mytre, set forth with the signe of hoolynesse, the glorie of onour, and the werk of vertu, ourned to desijr of iyen.
45.13: Siche thingis so faire weren not bifore hym, `til to the eest.
45.14: Noon alien was clothid ther ynne, but oneli hise sones, and hise sones sones aloone, bi al tyme.
45.15: Hise sacrifices weren endid ech dai bi fyer. Moises fillide hise hondis, and anoyntide hym with hooli oile. It was maad to hym in to euerlastynge testament, and to his seed as the daies of heuene, to vse presthod, and to haue preisyng, and to glorifie his puple in his name.
45.16: God chees hym of ech lyuynge man, to offre sacrifice to God, encense, and good odour, in to mynde, for to plese for his puple.
45.17: And he yaf to hym power in hise comaundementis, and in the testamentis of domes, to teche Jacob witnessyngis, and in his lawe to yyue liyt to Israel.
45.18: For aliens stooden ayens hym, and men that weren with Datan and Abiron, and the congregacioun of Chore, in wrathfulnesse cumpassiden hym for enuye, in desert.
45.19: The Lord siy, and it pleside not hym; and thei weren wastid in the feersnesse of wrathfulnesse. He made to hem wondris ayens kynde, and in the flawme of fier he wastide hem.
45.20: And he encreesside glorie to Aaron, and yaf eritage to hym; and he departide to Aaron the firste thingis of fruytis of the erthe.
45.21: He made redi his breed in the firste thingis, in to fulnesse; for whi and thei shulen ete the sacrifices of the Lord, whiche he yaf to hym, and to his seed.
45.22: But in the lond of his folk he schal not haue eritage, and no part is to hym among the folk; for whi God is the part and eritage of hym.
45.23: Fynees, the sone of Eleazarus, was the thridde in glorie, in suynge hym in the drede of God, and to stonde in the reuerence of folk; in the goodnesse and gladnesse of his soule he pleside God of Israel.
45.24: Therfor God ordeynede to hym the testament of pees, and made hym prince of hooli men, and of his folk; that the dignete of presthod be to hym and to his seed, with outen ende.
45.25: And the testament of Dauid, the sone of Jesse, of the lynage of Juda, was eritage to hym, and to his seed; that he schulde yyue wisdom in to oure herte, to deme his folk in riytfulnesse, lest her goodis schulen be don awei; and he made the glorie of hem to be euerlastinge, in the folk of hem.

46.1: Jhesus Naue, the successour of Moises in profetis, was strong in batel, that was greet bi his name. The gretteste in to the helthe of chosun men of God, to ouercome enemyes risynge ayens hem, that he schulde gete the erytage of Israel.
46.2: Which glorie he gat in reysynge his hondis, and in castynge scharpe arowis ayens citees.
46.3: Who bifore hym ayenstood so? for whi the Lord hym silf smoot the enemyes.
46.4: Whether the sunne was not lettid in the wrathfulnesse of hym, and o dai was maad as tweyne?
46.5: He clepide to help the hiyeste God, myyti in ouercomynge enemyes on ech side; and God, greet and hooli, herde hym, in stoonys of hail of ful greet vertu.
46.6: He made asauyt ayens the folk enemy, and in the comynge doun he loste the aduersaries; that hethene men knowe the myyt of hym, for it is not esy to fiyte ayens the Lord; and he suede myyti men at the bak.
46.7: And in the daies of Moises he and Caleph, the sone of Jephone, diden merci; to stonde ayens the enemye, and to forbede the folk fro synnes, and to refreyne the grutchyng of malice.
46.8: And thei tweyne weren stidfast, and weren delyuered fro perel, of the noumbre of sixe hundrid thousynde `foot men, to brynge hem in to the eritage, in to the lond that flowith mylk and hony.
46.9: And the Lord yaf strengthe to thilke Caleph, and til in to elde vertu dwellide perfitli to hym; that he stiede in to the hiy place of the lond, and his seed gat eritage.
46.10: And alle the children of Israel sien, that it is good to obeie to hooli God.
46.11: And alle iugis bi her name, the herte of whiche was not corrupt, weren strong in batel, which weren not turned awei fro the Lord;
46.12: that the mynde of hem be in blessyng, and her boonys apperen fro her place; and her name dwellith with outen ende, for the glorie of hooli men dwellith at the sones of hem.
46.13: Samuel, the profete of the Lord, that was louyd of his Lord God, made newe the empire, and anoyntide prynces in his folk.
46.14: In the lawe of the Lord he demyde the congregacioun, and he siy the Lord of Jacob, and in his feith he was preued a profete.
46.15: And he was knowun feithful in hise wordis, for he siy the Lord of liyt.
46.16: And he clepide in to help the Lord almyyti, in ouercomynge enemyes stondynge aboute on ech side, in the offrynge of a man vndefoulid.
46.17: And the Lord thundride fro heuene, and in greet soun he made his vois herd.
46.18: And he al to-brak the princes of men of Tyre, and alle the duykis of Filisteis.
46.19: And bifore the tyme of ende of his lijf, and of the world, he yaf witnessyng in the siyt of the Lord, and of Crist; he took not of ony man richessis, yhe, til to schoon; and no man accuside hym.
46.20: And after this he slepte, and he made knowun to the kyng, and he schewide to hym the ende of his lijf; and he enhaunside his vois fro the erthe in profesie, to do awei the wickidnesse of the folc.

47.1: Aftir these thingis Nathan, the profete, roos, in the daies of Dauid.
47.2: And as ynnere fatnesse departide fro the fleisch, so Dauid fro the sones of Israel.
47.3: He pleiede with liouns, as with lambren; he dide in lijk maner with beris, as with lambren of scheep.
47.4: Whether in his yongthe he killide not a giaunt, and took awei schenschip fro the folk? In reisynge the hond in a stoon of a slynge, he castide doun the ful out ioiyng of Golias,
47.5: where he clepide to help the Lord almyyti; and he yaf in his riyt hond to do awei a stronge man in batel, and to enhaunse the horn of his folk.
47.6: So he glorifiede hym in ten thousynde, and he preiside hym in the blessyngis of the Lord, in offrynge to hym the coroun of glorie.
47.7: For he al to-brak enemyes on ech side, and drow out bi the roote Filisteis contrarie, `til in to this dai; he al to-brak the horn of hem, `til in to with outen ende.
47.8: Dauid in ech werk yaf knouleching to hooli God, and hiy in the word of glorie. Of al his herte he heriede God, and he louyde the Lord that made hym, and yaf to hym power ayens enemyes.
47.9: And he made syngeris to stonde ayens the auter; and he made swete motetis in the soun of hem.
47.10: And he yaf fairnesse in halewyngis, and he ournede tymes `til to the endyng of lijf; that thei schulden preise the hooli name of the Lord, and make large eerli the hoolynesse of God.
47.11: Crist purgide the synnes of hym, and enhaunside his horn with outen ende; and he yaf to hym the testament of kyngis, and the seete of glorie in Israel.
47.12: Aftir hym roos a witti sone; and for hym he castide doun al the power of enemyes.
47.13: Salomon regnede in the daies of pees, to whom God made suget alle enemyes, that he schulde make an hous in the name of God, and make redi hoolynesse with outen ende, as he was lerned in his yongthe.
47.14: And he was fillid with wisdom as a flood is fillid; and his soule vnhilide the erthe.
47.15: And thou, Salomon, fillidist derk figuratif spechis in licnessis; and thi name was pupplischid to ilis afer, and thou were louyde in thi pees.
47.17: Londis wondriden in songis, and in prouerbis, and in licnessis, and interpretyngis, ether exposiciouns; and in the name of the Lord,
47.18: to whom the surname is God of Israel. Thou gaderidist togidere gold as latoun, and thou fillidist siluer as leed.
47.19: And thou bouwidist thi thies to wymmen; thou haddist power in thi bodi.
47.20: Thou hast youe a wem in thi glorie, and madist vnhooli thi seed, to brynge in wrathfulnesse to thi children, and thi foli in othere men;
47.21: that thou schuldist make the rewme departid in to tweyne, and of Effrem to comaunde an hard comaundement.
47.22: But God schal not forsake his merci, and schal not distrie, nether do awei hise werkis, nether he schal leese fro generacioun the sones sones of his chosun kyng Dauid; and he schal not distrie the seed of hym that loueth the Lord. Forsothe God yaf remenaunt to Jacob, and to Dauid of that generacioun. And Salomon hadde an ende with hise fadris.
47.23: And he lefte aftir hym of his seed Roboam, the foli of the folk, and made lesse fro prudence; which Roboam turnede awei the folk bi his councel. And Jeroboam, the sone of Nabath, that made Israel to do synne, and yaf to Effraym weie to do synne; and ful many synnes of hem weren plenteuouse,
47.24: for thei turneden hem awei greetli fro her lond.
47.25: And the lynage of Effraym souyte al wickidnessis, til defence cam to hem; and delyuerede hem fro alle synnes.

48.1: And Elie, the profete, roos as fier; for whi his word brente as a brond.
48.2: Which brouyte yn hungur on hem, and thei suynge hym weren maad fewe for enuye; for thei myyten not suffre the comaundementis of the Lord.
48.3: Bi the word of the Lord he held togidere heuene, and castide doun fro it fier to the erthe.
48.4: So Elie was alargid in his merueils; and who may haue glorie in lijk maner with thee, which tokist awei a deed man fro hellis,
48.5: fro the eritage of deth, in the word of the Lord God?
48.6: Which castidist doun kyngis to deth, and hast broke togidere liytli the power of hem, and gloriouse men fro her bed.
48.7: Which herdist dom in Syna, and in Oreb domes of defence.
48.8: Which anoyntist kyngis to penaunce, and makist prophetis successouris aftir thee.
48.9: Which were reseyued in a whirlwynde of fier, in a chare of horsis of fier.
48.10: Which art writun in the domes of tymes, to plese the wrathfulnesse of the Lord, to recounsele the herte of the fadir to the sone, and to restore the lynagis of Jacob.
48.11: Thei ben blessid, that siyen thee, and weren maad feir in thi frenschipe;
48.12: for whi we lyuen oneli in lijf, but after deth oure name schal not be siche. Elie, that was hilid in a whirlewynd; and his spirit was fillid in Elisee. Elisee in hise daies dredde not the prince, and no man ouercam hym bi power;
48.13: nether ony word ouercam hym, and his deed bodi profesiede.
48.14: In his lijf he dide wondris ayens kynde; and in deth he wrouyte merueilis.
48.15: In alle these thingis the puple dide not penaunce, and yeden not awei fro her synnes, til whanne thei weren cast awei fro her lond, and weren scatered in to ech lond. And a ful fewe folk was left, and a prince in the hous of Dauid.
48.16: Summe of hem diden that, that pleside God; but othere diden many synnes.
48.17: Ezechie maad strong his citee, and brouyte watir in to the myddis therof; and diggide a rooche with irun, and bildide a pit to watir.
48.18: In hise daies Senacherib stiede, and sente Rapsaces; and he reiside his hond ayens hem, and he reiside his hond ayens Syon, and was maad proud in his power.
48.19: Thanne the hertis and hondis of hem weren moued; and thei hadden sorewe as wymmen trauelynge of child.
48.20: And thei clepiden to help the merciful Lord, and thei spredden abrood the hondis, and reisiden to heuene; and the hooli Lord God herde soone the vois of hem. He hadde not mynde on her synnes, nether yaf hem to her enemyes; but he purgide hem in the hond of Isaie, the hooli profete.
48.21: The aungel of the Lord castide doun the castels of Assiriens, and al to-brak hem.
48.22: For whi Ezechie dide that that pleside the Lord, and yede strongli in the weie of Dauith, his fadir; which weie Isaie, the grete profete, and feithful in the siyt of God, comaundide to hym.
48.23: In the daies of hym the sunne yede ayen abak; and God encreesside lijf to the kyng.
48.24: With greet spirit Ysaie siy the laste thingis; and he coumfortide the moreneris in Sion, `in to with outen ende.
48.25: He schewide thingis to comynge, and hid thingis, bifore that tho camen.

49.1: The mynde of Josie maad in the makyng of odour, is the werk of a pyment makere. In ech mouth his mynde schal be maad swete as hony, and as musik in the feeste of wyn.
49.2: He was dressid of God in the penaunce of folk; and he took awei the abhomynaciouns of wickidnesse.
49.3: And the herte of hym gouernede to the Lord; and in the daies of synnes he strengthide pitee.
49.4: Outakun Dauid, Ezechie and Josie, alle kyngis diden synne. For whi the kyngis of Juda leften the lawe of myyti God, and dispisiden the drede of God.
49.5: For thei yauen her rewme to othere men, and her glorie to an alien folk.
49.6: Thei brenten the chosun citee of hoolynesse; and thei maden the weies therof forsakun in the hond of Jeremye.
49.7: For thei tretiden yuel hym, which from the wombe of the modir was halewid a profete, to turne vpsedoun, and to leese, and efte to bilde, and make newe.
49.8: Ezechiel, that siy the siyt of glorie, which the Lord schewide to hym in the chare of cherubyn.
49.9: For he made mynde of enemyes in reyn, to do wel to hem, that schewiden riytful weies.
49.10: And the boonys of twelue profetis apperen fro her place; and thei strengthiden Jacob, and ayenbouyten hem in the feith of her vertu.
49.11: Hou schulen we alarge Zorobabel? for whi and he was a signe in the riyt hond of God to Israel;
49.12: and Jhesu, the sone of Josedech? whiche in her daies bildiden an hous, and enhaunsiden the hooli temple to the Lord, maad redi in to euerlastynge glorie.
49.13: And Neemye in the mynde of myche tyme, that reiside to vs the wallis, `that weren cast doun, and made the yatis and lockis to stonde; which Neemye reiside oure housis.
49.14: No man borun in erthe was such as Enok; for whi and he was resseyued fro the erthe.
49.15: And Joseph, that was borun a man, the prince of britheren, the stidfastnesse of folk, the gouernour of britheren, the stablischyng of puple; and his boonys weren visitid, and profesieden after deth.
49.16: Seth and Sem, these gaten glorie anentis men, and ouer ech man in the generacioun of Adam.

50.1: Symount, the sone of Onyas, was a greet preest, which in his lijf vndursettide the hous, and in hise daies strengthide the temple.
50.2: Also the hiynesse of the temple was bildide of hym, the double bildyng, and hiy wallis of the temple.
50.3: In the daies of hym the pittis of watris camen forth; and as the see tho weren fillid aboue mesure.
50.4: Which Symount helide his folk, and delyuerede it fro perdicioun.
50.5: Which was myyti to alarge the citee; which gat glorie in the conuersacioun of folk; and alargide the entryng of the hous, and of the large cumpas aboute.
50.6: As the dai sterre in the myddis of a cloude, and as a ful moone schyneth in hise daies;
50.7: and as the sunne schynynge, so he schynede in the temple of God;
50.8: as a reyn bouwe schynynge among the cloudis of glorie, and as a flour of rosis in the daies of veer, and as lilies, that ben in the passyng of watir, and as encense smellynge in the daies of somer; as fier schynynge,
50.9: and ensence brennynge in fier; as a sad vessel of gold, ourned with ech preciouse stoon;
50.10: as an olyue tree spryngynge forth, and a cipresse tree reisynge it silf an hiy; while he took the stoole of glorie, and was clothid in the perfeccioun of vertu.
50.11: In the stiyng of the hooli auter, the clothing of hoolynesse yaf glorie.
50.12: Forsothe in takynge partis of the hoond of prestis, and he stood bisidis the auter. The coroun of britheren, as a plauntyng of cedre in the hil Liban, was aboute hym;
50.13: so thei stoden aboute hym as boowis of palm tree, and alle the sones of Aaron stoden in her glorie.
50.14: Sotheli the offryng of the Lord was in the hondis of hem, bifore al the synagoge of Israel; and he vside ful endyng on the auter, to alarge the offryng of the hiy kyng.
50.15: And he dresside his hond in moiste sacrifice; and sacrifiside in the blood of grape. He schedde out in the foundement of the auter, the odour of God to the hiy prince.
50.16: Thanne the sones of Aaron crieden lowde; thei sowneden in trumpis betun out with hameris, and maden a grete vois herd in to mynde bifore God.
50.17: Thanne al the puple hastiden togidere, and fellen doun on the face on the erthe, for to worschipe her Lord God, and to yyue preyers to almyyti God an hiy.
50.18: And men syngynge in her voices alargiden; and a soun ful of swetnesse was maad in the greet hous.
50.19: And the puple preiede the hiy Lord in preier, til that the onour of the Lord was doon perfitli, and thei parformeden her yifte.
50.20: Thanne Symount cam doun, and reiside hise hondis in to al the congregacioun of the sones of Israel, to yyue glorie to God bi hise lippis, and to haue glorie in the name of hym.
50.21: And he reherside his preier, willynge to schewe the vertu of God.
50.22: And he preyede more the Lord of alle, that made grete thingis in ech lond; which encreesside oure daies fro the wombe of oure modir, and dide with vs bi his mercy.
50.23: Yyue he gladnesse of herte to vs, and that pees be maad in Israel bi euerlastynge daies;
50.24: that Israel bileue, that Goddis merci is with vs, that he delyuere hem in her dayes.
50.25: Mi soule hatith twei folkis; but the thridde is not a folk, whom Y hate.
50.26: Thei that sitten in the hil of Seir, and the Filisteis, and the fonned puple, that dwellith in Sichemys.
50.27: Jhesus, the sone of Sirach, a man of Jerusalem, wroot in this book the techyng of wisdom, and of kunnyng; and he renulide wisdom of his herte.
50.28: He is blessid, that dwellith in these goodis; he that settith tho in his herte, schal euere be wijs.
50.29: For if he doith these thingis, he schal be miyti to alle thingis; for whi the liyt of God is the step of hym. Lord kyng, Y schal knouleche to thee; and Y schal togidere herie thee, my sauyour.

51.1: Y schal knouleche to thi name, for thou art maad an helpere and defendere to me;
51.2: and thou hast delyuered my bodi fro perdicioun, fro the snare of a wickid tunge, and fro the lippis of hem that worchen a leesyng; and in the siyt of hem that stonden nyy thou art maad an helpere to me.
51.3: And thou hast delyuered me, bi the multitude of merci of thi name, fro roreris maad redi to mete; fro the hondis of hem that souyten my soule, and fro many tribulaciouns that cumpassiden me; fro ouerleiyng of flawme that cumpasside me, and in the myddis of fier Y was not brent;
51.4: fro the depthe of the wombe of helle, and fro a tunge defoulyd, and fro a word of leesyng; fro a wickid kyng, and fro a tunge vniust.
51.5: `Til to the deth my soule schal preise thee, Lord;
51.6: and my lijf was neiyynge in helle bynethe.
51.7: Thei cumpassiden me on ech side, and noon was that helpide; Y was biholdynge to the help of men, and noon was.
51.8: Lord, Y hadde mynde on thi merci, and on thi worchyng togidere, that ben fro the world; for thou delyuerst hem that abiden thee, and thou delyuerst hem fro the hond of hethene men.
51.9: Thou enhaunsidist my dwellyng on erthe; and Y bisouyte for deth fletynge doun.
51.10: Y clepyde to help the Lord, fadir of my Lord, that he forsake not me in the dai of my tribulacioun, and forsake not me with outen help, in the tyme of hem that ben proude.
51.11: Y schal preise thi name contynueli, and Y schal herie it togidere in knoulechyng; and my preier is herd.
51.12: And thou hast delyuered me fro perdicioun, and thou hast delyuered me fro the wickid tyme. Therfor Y schal knouleche, and Y schal seie heriyng to thee; and Y schal blesse the name of the Lord.
51.13: Whanne yit Y was yongere, bifore that Y erride, Y souyte wisdom opynli in my preier.
51.14: Bifore the tyme of eelde Y axide for it, and `til in to the laste thingis Y schal enquere it; and it schal flour as a grape ripe bifore othere.
51.15: Myn herte was glad ther ynne, my foot yede a riytful weye; fro my yongthe Y souyte it.
51.16: Y bowide doun a litil myn eere, and Y took it.
51.17: Y foonde myche wisdom in my silf, and Y profitide myche ther ynne. Y schal yyue glorie to hym, that yyueth wisdom to me.
51.18: For whi Y took councel to do it; Y loued feruentli good, and Y schal not be schent.
51.19: My soule wrastlide togidere ther ynne; and Y was confermyd in doynge it. Y stretchide forth myn hondis an hiy; and my soule schynede in the wisdom of hym, and he liytnyde myn vnkunnyngis.
51.20: Y dresside my soule to it; and Y foond it in knowyng. Y hadde pesibli fro the bigynnyng an herte with tho; for this thing Y schal not be forsakun.
51.21: My soule was disturblid in sekynge it; therfor Y schal haue pesibli a good possessioun.
51.22: For whi the Lord yaf to me a tunge my meede; and in it Y schal preise hym.
51.23: Ye vntauyt men, neiye to me; and gadere ye you in to the hous of techyng.
51.24: What tarien ye yit? and what seien ye in these thingis? youre soules thristen greetli.
51.25: Y openyde my mouth, and Y spak, Bie ye wisdom to you with out siluer,
51.26: and make youre necke suget to the yok therof, and youre soule resseyue techyng; for whi it is in the nexte to fynde it.
51.27: Se ye with youre iyen, that Y trauelide a litil, and Y foond myche reste to me.
51.28: Take ye techyng in myche noumbre of siluere, and welde ye plenteuouse gold ther ynne.
51.29: Youre soule be glad in the merci of hym; and ye schulen not be schent in the preysing of hym.

1.1: And these ben the wordis of the book, which Baruk, the sone of Nerie, sone of Maasie, sone of Sedechie, sone of Sedei, sone of Helchie, wroot in Babilonye;
1.2: in the fyuethe yeer, in the seuenthe dai of the monethe, in the tyme wherynne Caldeis token Jerusalem, and brenten it with fier.
1.3: And Baruk redde the wordis of this book to the eeris of Jeconye, sone of Joachym, kyng of Juda, and to the eeris of al the puple comynge to the book;
1.4: and to the eeris of the myyti sones of kyngis, and to the eeris of prestis, and to the eeris of the puple, fro the mooste `til to the leeste of hem, of alle dwellynge in Babiloyne, and at the flood Sudi.
1.5: Whiche herden, and wepten, and fastiden, and preieden in the siyt of the Lord.
1.6: And thei gaderiden monei, bi that that ech mannus hond myyte;
1.7: and senten in to Jerusalem to Joachym, the prest, sone of Helchie, sone of Salen, and to the preestis, and to al the puple that weren foundun with hym in Jerusalem;
1.8: whanne he took the vessels of the temple of the Lord, that weren takun awei fro the temple, to ayen clepe in to the lond of Juda, in the tenthe dai of the monethe Siban; the siluerne vessels, which Sedechie, the kyng of Juda, the sone of Josie,
1.9: made, aftir that Nabugodonosor, kyng of Babiloyne, hadde take Jeconye, and princes, and alle myyti men, and the puple of the lond fro Jerusalem, and ledde hem boundun in to Babiloyne.
1.10: And thei seiden, Lo! we han sent to you richessis, of whiche bie ye brent sacrifices, and encense, and make ye sacrifice, and offre ye for synne at the auter of youre Lord God.
1.11: And preye ye for the lijf of Nabugodonosor, king of Babiloyne, and for the lijf of Balthasar, his sone, that the daies of hem ben on erthe as the daies of heuene;
1.12: that the Lord yyue vertu to vs, and liytne oure iyen, that we lyue vndur the schadewe of Nabugodonosor, kyng of Babiloyne, and vndur the schadewe of Balthasar, his sone; and that we serue hem bi many daies, and fynde grace in the siyt of hem.
1.13: And preye ye for `vs silf to our Lord God, for we han synned to oure Lord God, and his strong veniaunce is not turned awei fro vs, `til in to this dai.
1.14: And rede ye this book, which we senten to you, to be rehersid in the temple of the Lord, in a solempne dai, and in a couenable dai.
1.15: And ye schulen seie, Riytfulnesse is to oure Lord God, but schenschipe of oure face is to vs, as this dai is, to al Juda, and to dwelleris in Jerusalem,
1.16: to oure kyngis, and to oure princes, to oure preestis, and to oure profetis, and to oure fadris.
1.17: We synneden bifor oure Lord God, and bileuyden not, and tristiden not in hym.
1.18: And we weren not redi to be suget to hym, and we obeiden not to the vois of oure Lord God, that we yeden in hise comaundementis, whiche he yaf to vs;
1.19: fro the dai in which he ledde oure fadris out of the lond of Egipt, til in to this dai, we weren vnbileueful to oure Lord God; and we weren scaterid, and yeden awei, that we herden not the vois of hym.
1.20: And many yuels and cursyngis, whiche the Lord ordeynede to his seruaunt Moises, cleuyden to vs; which Lord ledde oure fadris out of the lond of Egipt, to yyue to vs a lond flowynge mylk and hony, as in this dai.
1.21: And we herden not the vois of oure Lord God, bi alle the wordis of prophetis, whiche he sente to vs, and to oure iugis;
1.22: and we yeden awei, ech man in to the wit of his yuel herte, to worche to alien goddis, and we diden yuels bifore the iyen of oure Lord God.

2.1: For which thing oure Lord God settide stidfastli his word, which he spak to vs, and to oure iugis, that demyden in Israel, and to oure kyngis, and to oure princes, and to al Israel and Juda;
2.2: that the Lord schulde brynge on vs grete yuels, that weren not don vndur heuene, as tho ben doon in Jerusalem; bi tho thingis that ben writun in the lawe of Moises,
2.3: that a man schulde ete the fleischis of his sone, and the fleischis of his douyter.
2.4: And he yaf hem in to the hond of alle kyngis, that ben in oure cumpas, in to schenschipe, and in to desolacioun in alle puplis, among whiche the Lord scateride vs.
2.5: And we ben maad bynethe, and not aboue; for we synneden to oure Lord God, in not obeiynge to the vois of hym.
2.6: Riytfulnesse is to oure Lord God, but schenschipe of face is to vs and to oure fadris, as this dai is.
2.7: For the Lord spak on vs alle these yuels, that camen on vs.
2.8: And we bisouyten not the face of oure Lord God, that we schulden turne ayen, ech of vs fro oure worste weies.
2.9: And the Lord wakide in yuels, and brouyte tho on vs; for the Lord is iust in alle hise werkis, whiche he comaundide to vs.
2.10: And we herden not the vois of hym, that we schulden go in the comaundementis of the Lord, whiche he yaf bifore oure face.
2.11: And now, Lord God of Israel, that leddist thi puple out of the lond of Egipt in a strong hond, and in myraclis, and in grete wondris, and in thi greet vertu, and in an hiy arm, and madist to thee a name, as this dai is;
2.12: we han synned, we han do vnfeithfuli, we han do wickidli, oure Lord God, in alle thi riytfulnessis.
2.13: Thi wrath be turned awey fro vs; for we ben left a fewe among hethene men, where thou scateridist vs.
2.14: Lord, here thou oure axyngis, and oure preyeris, and lede vs out for thee; and yyue thou to vs to fynde grace bifore the face of hem, that ledden vs awei;
2.15: that al erthe knowe, that thou art oure Lord God, and that thi name is clepid to help on Israel, and on the kyn of hym.
2.16: Lord, bihold thou fro thin hooli hous on vs, and bouwe doun thin eere, and here vs.
2.17: Opene thin iyen, and se; for not deed men that ben in helle, whos spirit is takun fro her entrails, schulen yyue onour and iustefiyng to the Lord;
2.18: but a soule which is sori on the greetnesse of yuel, and goith bowid, and sijk, and iyen failynge, and an hungri soule, yyueth glorie to thee, and riytfulnesse to the Lord.
2.19: For not bi the riytfulnesses of oure fadris we `scheden merci bifore thi siyt, oure Lord God;
2.20: but for thou sentist thi wraththe and thi stronge veniaunce on vs, as thou spakest in the hondis of thi children profetis,
2.21: and seidist, Thus seith the Lord, Bowe ye youre schuldur, and youre necke, and do ye trauel to the kyng of Babiloyne; and ye schulen sitte in the lond, which Y yaf to youre fadris.
2.22: That if ye don not, nethir heren the vois of youre Lord God, to worche to the kyng of Babiloyne, Y schal make youre failyng fro the citees of Juda, and fro the yatis of Jerusalem;
2.23: and Y schal take awei fro you the vois of gladnesse, and the vois of ioye, and the vois of spouse, and the vois of spousesse; and al the lond schal be with out step of hem that dwellen therynne.
2.24: And thei herden not thi vois, that thei schulden worche to the kyng of Babiloyne; and thou hast set stidfastli thi wordis, whiche thou spakist in the hondis of thi children, prophetis; that the boonys of oure kyngis, and the boonys of oure fadris schulen be borun ouer fro her place.
2.25: And lo! tho ben cast forth in the heete of the sunne, and in the frost of niyt; and men ben deed in the worste sorewis, in hungur, and in swerd, and in sending out.
2.26: And thou hast set the temple in which thi name was clepid to help, as this dai schewith, for the wickidnesse of the hous of Israel, and of the hous of Juda.
2.27: And thou, oure Lord God, hast do in vs bi al thi goodnesse, and bi al that greet merciful doyng of thee,
2.28: as thou spakest in the hond of thi child Moises, in the dai in which thou comaundidist to hym to write thi lawe bifore the sones of Israel, and seidist,
2.29: If ye heren not my vois, this greet ournyng and myche schal be turned in to the leest among hethene men, whidur Y schal scatere hem.
2.30: For Y woot, that the puple schal not here me, for it is a puple of hard nol. And it schal turne to her herte in the lond of her caitiftee;
2.31: and thei schulen wite, that Y am the Lord God of hem. And Y schal yyue to hem an herte, and thei schulen vndurstonde, and eeris, and thei schulen here.
2.32: And thei schulen herie me in the lond of her caitiftee, and thei schulen be myndeful of my name.
2.33: Thei schulen turne awei hem silf fro her hard bak, and fro her wickidnessis; for thei schulen haue mynde of the wei of her fadris, that synneden ayens me.
2.34: And Y schal ayen clepe hem in to the lond, which Y swoor to yyue to the fadris of hem, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and thei schulen be lordis of it. And Y schal multiplie hem, and thei schulen not be maad lesse.
2.35: And Y schal ordeyne to hem an other testament euerlastynge, that Y be to hem in to God, and thei schulen be to me in to a puple. And Y schal no more moue my puple, the sones of Israel, fro the lond which Y yaf to hem.

3.1: And now, Lord almiyti, God of Israel, a soule in angwischis and a spirit anoied crieth to thee.
3.2: Lord, here thou, and haue merci, for thou art merciful God; and haue thou merci on vs, for we han synned bifor thee,
3.3: that sittist withouten ende, and we schulen not perische withouten ende.
3.4: Lord God almiyti, God of Israel, here thou now the preier of the deed men of Israel, and of the sones of hem, that synneden bifor thee, and herden not the vois of her Lord God, and yuels ben fastned to vs.
3.5: Nyle thou haue mynde on the wickidnesse of oure fadris, but haue thou mynde on thin hond and on thi name in this tyme;
3.6: for thou art oure Lord God, and, Lord, we schulen herie thee.
3.7: For whi for this thing thou hast youe thi drede in oure hertis, that we clepe thi name to help, and herie thee in oure caitiftee; for we schulen be conuertid fro the wickidnesse of oure fadris, that synneden ayens thee.
3.8: And lo! we ben in oure caitifte to dai, whidur thou scateridist vs, in to schenschipe, and in to cursyng, and in to synne, bi al the wickidnesse of oure fadris, that yeden awei fro thee, thou oure Lord God.
3.9: Israel, here thou the comaundementis of lijf; perseyue thou with eeris, that thou kunne prudence.
3.10: Israel, what is it, that thou art in the lond of enemyes?
3.11: Thou wexidist eld in an alien lond, thou art defoulid with deed men, thou art arettid with hem, that goon doun in to helle?
3.12: Thou hast forsake the welle of wisdom;
3.13: for whi if thou haddist gon in the weies of God, sotheli thou haddist dwellid in pees on erthe.
3.14: Lerne thou, where is wisdom, where is prudence, where is vertu, where is vndurstondyng, that thou wite togidere, where is long duryng of lijf and lijf lode, where is liyt of iyen, and pees.
3.15: Who foond the place therof, and who entride in to the tresouris therof?
3.16: Where ben the princes of hethene men, and that ben lordis ouer the beestis, that ben on erthe?
3.17: Whiche pleien with the briddis of heuene;
3.18: whiche tresoren siluer and gold, in which men tristen, and noon ende is of the purchasyng of hem? Which maken siluer, and ben busi, and no fyndyng is of her werkis?
3.19: Thei ben distried, and yeden doun to hellis; and othere men riseden in the place of hem.
3.20: The yonge men of hem sien liyt, `and dwelliden on erthe. But thei knewen not the weie of wisdom, nether vndurstoden the pathis therof;
3.21: nether the sones of hem resseyueden it. It was maad fer fro the face of hem;
3.22: it is not herd in the lond of Canaan, nether is seyn in Theman.
3.23: Also the sones of Agar, that souyten out prudence which is of erthe, the marchauntis of erthe, and of Theman, and the tale telleris, and sekeris out of prudence and of vndurstondyng. But thei knewen not the weie of wisdom, nether hadden mynde on the paththis therof.
3.24: O! Israel, the hous of God is ful greet, and the place of his possessioun is greet;
3.25: it is greet and hath noon ende, hiy and greet without mesure.
3.26: Namyd giauntis weren there; thei that weren of greet stature at the bigynnyng, and knewen batel.
3.27: The Lord chees not these, nether thei founden the weie of wisdom; therfor thei perischiden.
3.28: And for thei hadden not wisdom, thei perischiden for her vnwisdom.
3.29: Who stiede in to heuene, and took that wisdom, and brouyte it doun fro the cloudis?
3.30: Who passide ouer the see, and foond it, and brouyte it more than chosun gold?
3.31: Noon is, that mai knowe the weie therof, nethir that sekith the pathis therof;
3.32: but he that han alle thingis, knewe it, and foond it bi his prudence. Which made redi the erthe in euerlastynge tyme, and fillide it with twei footid beestis, and foure footid beestis.
3.33: Which sendith out liyt, and it goith, and clepide it; and it obeieth to hym in tremblyng.
3.34: Forsothe sterris yauen liyt in her kepyngis, and weren glad; tho weren clepid, and tho seiden, We ben present; and tho schyneden to hym with mirthe, that made tho.
3.35: This is oure God, and noon other schal be gessid ayens hym.
3.36: This foond ech weie of wisdom, and yaf it to Jacob, his child, and to Israel, his derlyng.
3.37: Aftir these thingis he was seyn in londis, and lyuede with men.

4.1: This book of Goddis heestis, and the lawe which is withouten ende. Alle that holden it, schulen come to lijf. But thei that han forsake it, schulen come in to deth.
4.2: Jacob, be thou conuertid, and take thou it; go thou bi the weie at the briytnesse therof, ayens the liyt therof. Yyue thou not thi glorie to another, and thi dignyte to an alien folc. Israel, we ben blessid; for tho thingis that plesen God, ben open to vs.
4.5: The puple of God, Israel worthi to be had in mynde, be thou `of betere coumfort.
4.6: Ye ben seeld to hethene men, not in to perdicioun; but for that that ye in ire terreden God to wrathfulnesse, ye ben bitakun to aduersaries.
4.7: For ye wraththiden thilke God euerlastynge, that made you; and ye offriden to fendis, and not to God.
4.8: For ye foryaten hym that nurschide you, and ye maden sori youre nurse, Jerusalem.
4.9: For it siy wrathfulnesse of God comynge to you, and it seide, Ye niy coostis of Sion, here; forsothe God hath brouyte greet morenyng to me.
4.10: For Y siy the caitiftee of my puple, of my sones and douytris, which he that is with out bigynnyng and ende brouyte on hem.
4.11: For Y nurschide hem with myrthe; but Y lefte hem with wepyng and morenyng.
4.12: No man haue ioye on me, a wedewe and desolat. Y am forsakun of manye for the synnes of my sones; for thei bowiden awei fro the lawe of God.
4.13: Forsothe thei knewen not `the riytfulnessis of hym; nether thei yeden bi the weies of Goddis heestis, nether bi the pathis of his treuthe thei entriden with riytfulnesse.
4.14: The niy coostis of Sion come, and haue thei mynde on the caitifte of my sones and douytris, which he that is with out bigynnyng and ende brouyte on hem.
4.15: For he brouyte on hem a folk fro fer, an yuel folk, and of an other langage;
4.16: that reuerensiden not an eld man, nether hadden merci on children; and thei ledden awei the dereworthe sones of a widewe, and maden a womman aloone desolat of sones.
4.17: But what mai Y helpe you?
4.18: For he that brouyte on you yuels, shal delyuer you fro the hondis of youre enemyes.
4.19: Go ye, sones, go ye; for Y am forsakun aloone. Y haue vnclothid me of the stoole of pees; but Y haue clothid me with a sak of bisechyng, and Y schal crie to the hiyeste in my daies.
4.21: Sones, be ye of betere comfort; crie ye to the Lord, and he schal delyuere you fro the hond of princes, that ben youre enemyes.
4.22: For Y hopide youre helthe with outen ende, and ioye cam to me fro the hooli on merci, that schal come to you fro youre sauyour without bigynnyng and ende.
4.23: For Y sente you out with mourenyng and wepyng; but God schal brynge you ayen to me with ioye and myrthe with outen ende.
4.24: For as the neiyboressis of Sion sien youre caitifte maad of God, so thei schulen se and in swiftnesse youre helthe of God, which helthe schal come to you fro aboue with greet onour and euerlastynge schynyng.
4.25: Sones, suffre ye pacientli ire, that cam on you; for thin enemy pursuede thee, but thou schalt se soone the perdicioun of hym, and thou schalt stie on the neckes of hym.
4.26: My delicat men yeden scharp weies; for thei as a floc `that is rauyschid weren led of enemyes.
4.27: Sones, be ye pacientere, and crie ye fer to the Lord; for whi youre mynde schal be of hym that ledith you.
4.28: For as youre wit was, that ye erriden fro God, ye schulen conuerte eft, and schulen seke hym tensithis so myche.
4.29: For he that brouyte in yuels to you, schal brynge eft euerlastynge myrthe to you with youre helthe.
4.30: Jerusalem, be thou of betere coumfort; for he that nemyde thee, excitith thee.
4.31: Thei that traueliden thee, schulen perische gilti; and thei that thankiden in thi fallyng, schulen be punyschid.
4.32: Citees to which thi sones serueden, `schulen be punyschid, and that citee that took thi sones, schal be punyschid.
4.33: For as Babiloyne made ioie in thi hurlyng doun, and was glad in thi fal, so it schal be maad sori in his desolacioun.
4.34: And the ful out ioye of the multitude therof schal be kit awei, and the ioie therof schal be in to mourenyng.
4.35: For whi fier schal come on it fro hym that is without bigynnyng and ende, in ful long daies; and it schal be enhabitid of fendis, in to the multitude of tyme.
4.36: Jerusalem, biholde aboute to the eest, and se thou myrthe comynge of God to thee.
4.37: For lo! thi sones comen, which thou leftist scatered; thei comen gaderid fro the eest `til to the west in the word of the hooli, and maken ioie to the onour of God.

5.1: Jerusalem, vnclothe thee of the stoole of thi mourenyng, and trauelyng; and clothe thou thee in the fairnesse, and onour of it, which is of God to thee in euerlastynge glorie.
5.2: God of ryytfulnesse schal cumpasse thee with a double cloth, and schal sette on thin heed a mytre of euerlastynge onour.
5.3: For God schal schewe his briytnesse in thee, which is vndur heuene.
5.4: For thi name schal be namyd of God to thee with outen ende, The pees of riytfulnesse, and the onour of pitee.
5.5: Jerusalem, rise vp, and stonde in an hiy place, and biholde aboute to the eest; and se thi sones gaderid togidere fro the sunne risynge til to the west in the word of the hooli, that maken ioie in the mynde of God.
5.6: For thei yeden out fro thee, and weren led of enemyes on feet; but the Lord schal brynge to thee hem borun in to honour, as the sones of rewme.
5.7: For God hath ordeyned to make low ech hiy hil, and euerlastynge rochis of stoon, and gret valeis, to fille the uneuenesse of erthe; that Israel go diligentli in to the onour of God.
5.8: Forsothe wodis and ech tree of swetnesse schadewiden Israel, bi the comaundement of God.
5.9: For God schal brynge Israel with mirthe in the liyt of his maieste, with merci and riytfulnesse, which is of hym.

6.1: For the synnes which ye synneden bifor God, ye schulen be led prisoneris in to Babiloyne, of Nabugodonosor, kyng of Babiloynes.
6.2: Therfor ye schulen entre in to Babiloyne, and ye schulen be there ful many yeeris, and in to long tyme, til to seuene generaciouns; forsothe after this Y schal lede out you fro thennus with pees.
6.3: But now ye schulen se in Babiloyne goddis of gold, and of siluer, and of stoon, and of tree, to be borun on schuldris, schewynge drede to hethene men.
6.4: Therfor se ye, lest also ye be maad lijk alien dedis, and lest ye dreden, and drede take you in hem.
6.5: Therfor whanne ye seen a cumpeny bihynde and bifore, worschipe ye God, and seie in youre hertes, Lord God, it bihoueth that thou be worschipid.
6.6: Forsothe myn aungel is with you, but Y schal seke youre soulis.
6.7: For whi the trees of hem ben polischid of a carpenter; also tho ben araied with gold, and araied with siluer, and ben false, and moun not speke.
6.8: And as to a virgyn louynge ournementis, so, whanne gold is takun, ourenementis ben maad to idols.
6.9: Certis the goddis of hem han goldun corouns on her heedis; wherfor prestis withdrawen fro tho goddis gold and siluer, and spenden it in hem silf.
6.10: Sotheli thei yyuen also of that to hooris, and araien hooris; and eft whanne thei resseyuen that of hooris, thei araien her goddis.
6.11: But tho goddis ben not delyuered fro rust and mouyte.
6.12: Forsothe whanne `tho goddis ben hilid with a cloth of purpure, preestis schulen wipe the face of tho, for dust of the hous, which is ful myche among tho goddis.
6.14: Forsothe idols han a septre, as a man hath; as the iuge of a cuntrei, that sleeth not a man synnynge ayens him silf.
6.15: Also tho han in the hond a swerd, and ax; but tho delyueren not hem silf fro batel and fro theues. Wherfor be it knowun to you, that tho ben not goddis;
6.17: therfor worschipe ye not tho. For as a brokun vessel of a man is maad vnprofitable, siche also ben the goddis of hem. Whanne tho ben set in the hous, the iyen of tho ben ful of dust of the feet of men entrynge.
6.18: And as yatis ben set aboute a man that offendide the kyng, ether as whanne a deed man is brouyt to the sepulcre, so preestis kepen sikirli the doris with closyngis and lockis, lest tho be robbid of theuys.
6.19: Thei teenden lanternes to tho, and sotheli many lanternes, of which tho moun se noon; forsothe tho ben as beemes in an hous.
6.20: Sotheli men seien that serpentis, that ben of erthe, licken out the hertis of tho; while the serpentis eten tho, and her cloth, and tho feelen not.
6.21: The faces of tho ben blake of the smoke, which is maad in the hous.
6.22: Nyyt crowis and swalewis fleen aboue the bodi of tho, and aboue the heed of tho, and briddis also, and cattis in lijk maner.
6.23: Wherfor wite ye, that tho ben not goddis; therfor drede ye not tho.
6.24: Also the gold which tho han, is to fairnesse; no but summan wipe awei the rust, tho schulen not schyne. For tho feliden not, the while tho weren wellid togidere.
6.25: Tho ben bouyt of al prijs, in which no spirit is in tho.
6.26: Tho without feet ben borun on schuldris of men, and schewen opynli her vnnoblei to men; be thei schent also that worschipen tho.
6.27: Therfor if tho fallen doun to erthe, tho schulen not rise of hem silf; and if ony man settith that idol upriyt, it schal not stonde bi it silf, but as to deed thingis schuldris schulen be put to tho.
6.28: The prestis of tho sillen the sacrifices of tho, and mysvsen; in lijk maner and the wymmen of hem rauyschen awei, nether to a sijk man, nether to a begger tho yyuen ony thing.
6.29: Of her sacrifices foule wymmen, and in vncleene blood, touchen. Therfor wite ye bi these thingis, that tho ben not goddis, and drede ye not tho.
6.30: For wherof ben tho clepid goddis? For wymmen setten sacrifices to goddis of siluer, and of gold, and of tre;
6.31: and preestis that han cootis to-rent, and heedis and berd schauun, whos heedis ben nakid, sitten in the housis of tho.
6.32: Sotheli thei roren and crien ayens her goddis, as in the soper of a deed man.
6.33: Prestis taken awei the clothis of tho, and clothen her wyues, and her children. And if tho suffren ony thing of yuel of ony man,
6.34: ether if tho suffren ony thing of good, tho moun not yelde. Nether tho moun ordeyne a kyng, nethir do awei.
6.35: In lijk maner tho moun nether yyue richessis, nether yilde yuel. If ony man makith a vow to tho, and yeldith not, tho axen not this.
6.36: Tho delyueren not a man fro deth, nether rauyschen a sijk man fro a miytiere.
6.37: Tho restoren not a blynd man to siyt; tho schulen not delyuere a man fro nede.
6.38: Tho schulen not haue merci on a widewe, nether tho schulen do good to fadirles children.
6.39: Her goddis of tre, and of stoon, and of gold, and of siluer, ben lijk stoonys of the mounteyn; forsothe thei that worschipen tho, schulen be schent. Hou therfor is it to gesse, ether to seie,
6.40: that tho ben goddis? for whi yit whanne Caldeis onouren not tho. Which whanne thei heren that a doumb man mai not speke, offren hym to Bel, and axen of hym to speke;
6.41: as if thei that han no stiryng, moun feel. And thei, whanne thei schulen vndurstonde, schulen forsake tho idols; for tho goddis of hem han no wit.
6.42: Forsothe wymmen gird with roopis sitten in weies, and kyndelen boonys of olyues.
6.43: Sotheli whanne ony of tho wymmen is drawun awei of ony man passynge, and slepith with hym, sche dispisith her neiyboresse, that sche is not hadde worthi as hir silf, nether hir roop is brokun.
6.44: Forsothe alle thingis that ben don to tho, ben false. Hou therfor is it to gesse, ethir to seie, that tho ben goddis?
6.45: Forsothe the idols ben maad of smithis, and of goldsmithis. Tho schulen be noon other thing, no but that that prestis wolen, that tho be.
6.46: Also thilke goldsmithis that maken tho, ben not of myche tyme; therfor whether tho thingis that ben maad of them moun be goddis?
6.47: Sotheli thei leften false thingis, and schenschipe to men to comynge aftirward.
6.48: For whi whanne batels and yuels comen on hem, preestis thenken, where thei schulen hide hem silf with tho.
6.49: Hou therfor owen tho to be demyd, that tho ben goddis, which nether delyueren hem silf fro batel, nether delyueren hem silf fro yuelis?
6.50: For whi whanne tho ben of tree, and of stoon, and of gold, and of siluer, it schal be knowun aftirward of alle folkis, and kyngis, that tho thingis ben false, that ben maad open; for tho ben not goddis, but the werkis of hondis of men, and no werk of God is with tho.
6.51: Wherof therfor it is knowun, that tho ben not goddis, but the werkis of hondis of men, and no werk of God is in tho.
6.52: Tho reisen not a kyng to a cuntrei, nether schulen yyue reyn to men.
6.53: Also tho schulen not deme doom, nether tho schulen delyuere the cuntrei fro wrong.
6.54: For tho moun no thing, as litle crowis bitwixe the myddis of heuene and of erthe. For whanne fier fallith in to the hous of goddis of tree, and of gold, and of siluer, sotheli the prestis of tho schulen fle, and schulen be delyuered; but tho schulen be brent as beemys in the myddis.
6.56: Forsothe tho schulen not ayen stonde a kyng and batel. Hou therfor is it to gesse, or to resseyue, that tho ben goddis?
6.57: Goddis of tree, and of stoon, and of gold and of siluer, schulen not delyuere hem silf fro nyyt theues, nether fro dai theuys, and wickid men ben strongere than tho goddis.
6.58: Thei schulen take awei gold, and siluer, and cloth, bi which tho ben hilid, and thei schulen go awei; nether tho helpen hem silf.
6.59: Therfor it is betere to be a kyng schewynge his vertu, ether a profitable vessel in the hous, in which he schal haue glorie that weldith it, than false goddis; ether a dore in the hous, that kepith tho thingis that ben in it, is betere than false goddis.
6.60: Forsothe the sunne, and moone, and sterris, whan tho ben briyt, and sent out to profitis, obeien.
6.61: In lijk maner and leit, whanne it apperith, is cleer. Sotheli the same thing and wynd brethith in ech cuntrei.
6.62: And cloudis, to whiche, whanne it is comaundid of God to go thorouy al the world, perfourmen that, that is comaundid to tho.
6.63: Also fier `that is sent fro aboue, to waste mounteyns and wodis, doith that, that is comaundid to it; but these idols ben not lijk to oon of tho thingis, nether bi fourmes, nether bi vertues.
6.64: Wherfor it is nether to gesse, nether to seie, that tho ben goddis, whanne tho moun not nether deme doom, nether do to men.
6.65: Therfor wite ye that tho ben not goddis, and drede ye not tho.
6.66: For tho schulen nether curse, nethir schulen blesse kyngis.
6.67: Also tho schewen not to hethene men signes in heuene, nether tho schulen schyne as the sunne, nether tho schulen yyue liyt as the moone.
6.68: Beestis that moun fle vndur a roof, and do profit to hem silf, ben betere than tho.
6.69: Therfor bi no maner it is open to you, that tho ben goddis.
6.70: For which thing drede ye not tho. For whi as `a bugge, either a man of raggis, in a place where gourdis wexen, kepith no thing, so ben her goddis of tree, and of siluer, and of gold.
6.71: In the same maner and a whijt thorn in a gardyn kepith no thing, on which thorn ech brid sittith, in lijk maner and her goddis of tree, and of gold, and of siluer, ben lijk a deed man cast forth in derknessis.
6.72: Also of purpur and of marble, whiche thei holden aboue it; therfor ye schulen wite, that tho ben not goddis. Also tho ben etun at the laste, and it schal be in to schenschipe in the cuntrei.

1.1: And thei walkiden in the myddis of the flawme, and herieden God, and blessiden the Lord.
1.2: Forsothe Asarie stoode, and preiede thus; and he openyde his mouth in the myddis of the fier,
1.3: and seide, Lord God of oure fadris, thou art blessid, and worthi to be heried, and thi name is glorious in to worldis;
1.4: for thou art riytful in alle thingis whiche thou didist to vs, and alle thi werkis ben trewe; and thi weies ben riytful, and alle thi domes ben trewe.
1.5: For thou hast do trewe domes, bi alle thingis whiche thou brouytist yn on vs, and on Jerusalem, the hooli citee of oure fadris; for in trewthe and in doom thou brouytist yn alle these thingis for oure synnes.
1.6: For we synneden, and diden wickidli, goynge awei fro thee, and we trespassiden in alle thingis,
1.7: and we herden not, nether kepten thi comaundementis, nether we diden as thou comaundidist to vs, that it schulde be wele to vs.
1.8: Therfor thou didist bi veri doom alle thingis whiche thou brouytist yn on vs, and alle thingis whiche thou didist to vs;
1.9: and thou hast bitake vs in the hondis of enemyes, wickid men, and worst trespassouris, and to the vniust kyng, and worst ouer al erthe.
1.10: And now we moun not opene the mouth; we ben maad schame and schenschipe to thi seruauntis, and to hem that worschipen thee.
1.11: We bisechen, yyue thou not vs to enemyes with outen ende, for thi name, and distrie thou not thi testament,
1.12: and take thou not awei thi merci fro vs, for Abraham, thi derlyng, and Ysaac, thi seruaunt, and Israel, thin hooli;
1.13: to whiche thou spakist, biheetyng that thou schuldist multiplie her seed as the sterris of heuene, and as grauel which is in the brynke of the see.
1.14: For whi, Lord, we ben maad litle, more than alle folkis, and we ben lowe in al erthe to dai, for oure synnes.
1.15: And in this tyme is no prince, and duyk, and profete, nether brent sacrifice, nether sacrifice, nether offryng, nether encense, nether place of firste fruytis bifor thee,
1.16: that we moun fynde thi mercy; but be we resseyued in contrit soule, and in spirit of mekenesse.
1.17: As in brent sacrifice of rammes, and of bolis, and as in thousyndis of fatte lambren, so oure sacrifice be maad to dai in thi siyt, that it plese thee; for no schame is to hem that tristen in thee.
1.18: And now we suen thee in al the herte, and we dreden thee, and we seken thi face.
1.19: Schende thou not vs, but do with vs bi thi myldenesse, and bi the multitude of thi merci.
1.20: And delyuere thou vs in thy merueils, and yyue thou glorie to thi name, Lord;
1.21: and alle men ben schent, that schewen yuelis to thi seruauntis; be thei schent in all thi miyt, and the strengthe of hem be al to-brokun;
1.22: and thei schulen wite, that thou art the Lord God aloone, and glorious on the roundnesse of londis.
1.23: And the mynystris of the kyng, that hadden sent hem, ceessiden not to make hoot the furneis with syment, and herdis of flex, and pitche, and siouns of vynes.
1.24: And the flawme was sched out ouer the furneis bi nyne and fourti cubitis,
1.25: and brak out, and brente hem that it foond of Caldeis bisidis the furneis.
1.26: Forsothe the aungel of the Lord cam doun with Asarie and hise felowis, in to the furneis, and smoot out the flawme of the fier fro the furneis;
1.27: and made the myddis of the furneis as the wynd of deew blowynge; and outerli the fier touchide not hem, nether made sori, nether dide ony thing of disese.
1.28: Thanne these thre as of o mouth herieden and glorifieden God, and blessiden God in the furneis,
1.29: and seiden, Lord God of oure fadris, thou art blessid, and worthi to be preisid, and gloriouse, and aboue enhaunsid in to worldis; and blessid is the name of thi glorie, which name is hooli, and worthi to be heried, and aboue enhaunsid in alle worldis.
1.30: Thou art blessid in the hooli temple of thi glorie, and aboue preisable, and gloriouse in to worldis.
1.31: Thou art blessid in the trone of thi rewme, and aboue preisable, and aboue enhaunsid in to worldis.
1.32: Thou art blessid, that biholdist depthis of watris, and sittist on cherubyn, and art preisable, and aboue enhaunsid in to worldis.
1.33: Thou art blessid in the firmament of heuene, and preisable, and gloriouse in to worldis.
1.34: Alle werkis of the Lord, blesse ye the Lord, herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.35: Aungels of the Lord, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.36: Heuenes, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.37: Alle watris, that ben aboue heuenes, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye him into worldis.
1.38: Alle the vertues of the Lord, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.39: Sunne and moone, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.40: Sterris of heuene, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.41: Reyn and deew, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.42: Ech spirit of God, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.43: Fier and heete, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.44: Coold and somer, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.45: Dewis and whijt forst, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.46: Blac forst and coold, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.47: Yces and snowis, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.48: Niytis and daies, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.49: Liyt and derknesse, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.50: Leitis and cloudis, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.51: The erthe blesse the Lord; herie it, and aboue enhaunse it hym in to worldis.
1.52: Mounteyns and litle hillis, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.53: Alle buriownynge thingis in erthe, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.54: Wellis, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.55: Sees and floodis, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.56: Whallis, and alle thingis that ben mouyd in watris, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.57: Alle briddis of the eyr, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.58: Alle wielde beestis and tame beestis, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.59: Sones of men, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.60: Israel blesse the Lord; herie it, and aboue enhaunse it hym in to worldis.
1.61: Prestis of the Lord, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.62: Seruauntis of the Lord, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.63: Spiritis and soulis of iust men, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.64: Hooli men and meke of herte, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis.
1.65: Ananye, Azarie, Mysael, blesse ye the Lord; herie ye, and aboue enhaunse ye hym in to worldis. Which Lord rauyschide vs fro helle, and `made saaf fro the hond of deth, and delyueride fro the myddis of flawme brennynge, and rauyschide vs fro the myddis of fier.
1.67: Knowleche ye to the Lord, for he is good; for his merci is in to the world.
1.68: Alle religiouse men, blesse ye the Lord, God of goddis; herie ye, and knouleche ye to hym, for his merci is in to alle worldis.

1.1: A man was in Babiloyne, and his name was Joachim.
1.2: And he took a wijf, Susanne bi name, the douyter of Helchie, a womman ful fair, and dredynge the Lord.
1.3: Forsothe hir fadir and modir, whanne thei weren riytful, tauyten her douyter bi the lawe of Moises.
1.4: Sotheli Joachim was ful riche, and he hadde a gardyn niy his hous; and the Jewis camen to hym, for he was the moost worschipful of alle.
1.5: And tweyne elde men weren ordeyned iugis in that yeer, of whiche the Lord spak, that wickidnesse yede out of Babiloyne, of the eldere iugis that semeden to gouerne the puple.
1.6: These iugis vsiden oft the hous of Joachym; and alle men that hadden domes camen to hem.
1.7: Forsothe whanne the puple hadde turned ayen after myddai, Susanne entride, and walkide in the gardyn of hir hosebonde.
1.8: And the eldre men siyen hir entrynge ech dai, and walkynge; and thei brenten out in to `the couetise of hir.
1.9: And thei turneden awei her wit, and bowiden doun her iyen, that thei siyen not heuene, nether bithouyten on iust domes.
1.10: Sotheli bothe weren woundid bi the loue of hir, and thei schewiden not her sorewe to hem silf togidere;
1.11: for thei weren aschamed to schewe to hem silf her coueitise, willynge to ligge fleischli bi hir.
1.12: And thei aspieden ech dai more bisili to se hir.
1.13: And oon seide to the tothir, Go we hoom, for the our of mete is. And thei yeden out, and departiden fro hem silf.
1.14: And whanne thei hadden turned ayen, thei camen in to o place; and thei axiden ech of othere the cause, and thei knoulechiden her coueitise. And thanne in comyn thei ordeyneden a tyme, whanne thei miyten fynde hir aloone.
1.15: Forsothe it was doon, whanne thei aspieden a couenable dai, sche entride sumtyme, as yistirdai and the thridde dai ago, with twei damysels aloone, and wolde be waischun in the gardyn; for whi heete was.
1.16: And no man was there, outakun tweyne elde men hid, biholdynge hir.
1.17: Therfor sche saide to the damysels, Bringe ye to me oile, and oynementis; and close ye the doris of the gardyn, that Y be waischun.
1.18: And thei diden as sche `hadde comaundid; and thei closiden the doris of the gardyn, and yeden out bi a posterne, to bringe tho thingis that sche hadde comaundid. And thei wisten not, that the elde men weren hid with ynne.
1.19: Sotheli whanne the damysels weren gon out, tweyne elde men risiden, and runnen to hir, and seiden, Lo!
1.20: the doris of the gardyn ben closid, and no man seeth vs, and we ben in `the coueitise of thee. Wherfor assente thou to vs, and be thou meddlid with vs.
1.21: That if thou wolt not, we schulen seie witnessyng ayens thee, that a yong man was with thee, and for this cause thou sentist out the damesels fro thee.
1.22: And Susanne inwardli sorewide, and seide, Angwischis ben to me on ech side; for if Y do this, deth is to me; forsothe if Y do not, Y schal not ascape youre hondis.
1.23: But it is betere for me to falle in to youre hondis without werk, than to do synne in the siyt of the Lord.
1.24: And Susanne criede `an hiy with greet vois, but also the elde men crieden ayens hir.
1.25: Forsothe oon ran, and openede the door of the gardyn.
1.26: Sotheli whanne the seruauntis of the hous hadden herd the cry in the gardyn, thei fellen in bi the posterne, to se what it was.
1.27: But after that the elde men spaken, the seruauntis weren aschamed greetly, for neuer was siche a word seid of Susanne. And the morew dai was maad.
1.28: And whanne the puple was comyn to Joachym, hir hosebonde, also the twei prestis fulle of wickid thouyte camen ayens Susanne, for to sle hir.
1.29: And thei seiden bifor al the puple, Sende ye to Susanne, the douyter of Helchie, the wijf of Joachym. And anoon thei senten.
1.30: And sche cam with hir fadir, and modir, and children, and alle kynesmen.
1.31: Certis Susanne was ful delicat, and fair of schap.
1.32: And tho wickid men comaundiden, that sche schulde be vnhilid, for sche was kyuered; that nameli so thei schuldun be fillid of hir fairnesse.
1.33: Therfor hir kynesmen wepten, and alle that knewen hir.
1.34: Forsothe the twei prestis risiden togidere in the myddis of the puple, and settiden her hondis on the heed of hir.
1.35: And sche wepte, and bihelde to heuene, and hir herte hadde trist in the Lord.
1.36: And the prestis seiden, Whanne we walkiden aloone in the gardyn, this Susanne entride with twei damesels; and sche closide the dore of the gardyn, and lefte the damesels.
1.37: And a yong man, that was hid, cam to hir, and lai bi hir.
1.38: Certis whanne we weren in a corner of the gardyn, we sien the wickidnesse, and runnen to hem, and we sien hem meddlid togidere.
1.39: And sotheli we myyten not take hym, for he was strongere than we; and whanne he hadde opened the doris, he skippide out.
1.40: But whanne we hadde take this womman, we axiden, who was the yonge man; and sche nolde schewe to vs. Of this thing we ben witnessis.
1.41: The multitude bileuede to hem, as to the eldre men and iugis of the puple, and condempneden hir to deth.
1.42: Forsothe Susanne criede loud with greet vois, and seide, Lord God, without bigynnyng and ende, that art knowere of hid thingis, that knowist alle thingis bifore that tho ben don;
1.43: thou wost, that thei han bore fals witnessyng ayens me. And lo! Y dye, whanne Y haue not do ony of these thingis, whiche these men han maad maliciously ayens me.
1.44: Forsothe the Lord herde the vois of hir.
1.45: And whanne she was led to the deth, the Lord reiside the hooli spirit of a yonge child, whos name was Danyel.
1.46: And he criede loude with a greet vois, Y am cleene of the blood of this womman.
1.47: And al the puple turned ayen to hym, and seide, What is this word, which thou hast spoke?
1.48: And whanne he stood in the myddis of hem, he seide, So ye, fonned children of Israel, not demynge nether knowynge that that is trewe, condempneden the douyter of Israel.
1.49: Turne ye ayen to the dom, for thei spaken fals witnessyng ayens hir.
1.50: Therfor the puple turnede ayen with haaste. And the elde men seiden to hym, Come thou, and sitte in the myddis of vs, and schewe to vs; for God hath youe to thee the onour of eelde.
1.51: And Danyel seide to hem, Departe ye hem atwynny fer, and Y schal deme hem.
1.52: Therfor, whanne thei weren departid oon fro the tother, he clepide oon of hem, and seide to hym, Thou elde man of yuel daies, now thi synnes ben comun, whiche thou wrouytist bifore,
1.53: demynge vniust domes, oppressynge innocentis, and delyuerynge gilti men, whanne the Lord seith, Thou schalt not sle an innocent and iust man.
1.54: But now if thou siest hir, seie thou, vndur what tree thou siest hem spekynge togidere to hem silf? Which seide, Vndur an haw tree.
1.55: Forsothe Danyel seide, Riytli thou liest in thin heed; for lo! the angel of the Lord, bi a sentence takun of hym, schal kitte thee bi the myddil.
1.56: And whanne he was stirid awei, he comaundide the tother to come, and seide to hym, Thou seed of Canaan, and not of Juda, fairnesse hath disseyued thee, and coueitise hath misturned thin herte;
1.57: thus ye diden to the douytris of Israel, and thei dredden, and spaken to you, but the douyter of Juda suffride not youre wickidnesse.
1.58: Now therfor seie thou to me, vndur what tree thou siest hem spekynge togidere to hem silf?
1.59: Which seide, Vndur a blak thorn. Forsothe Danyel seide to hym, Riytli also thou liest in thin heed; for the aungel of the Lord dwellith, and hath a swerd, that he kitte thee bi the myddil, and sle you.
1.60: Therfor al the puple criede lowde with greet vois, and blessiden `the Lord, that saueth hem that hopen in hym.
1.61: And thei risiden togidere ayens the twei preestis; for Danyel hadde conuyctid hem bi her mouth, that thei hadden bore fals witnessyng; and thei diden to hem, as thei hadden do yuele ayens the neiyboresse,
1.62: that thei schulden do bi the lawe of Moises, and thei killiden hem. And giltles blood was sauyd in that dai.
1.63: Forsothe Helchie and his wijf herieden the Lord in that day, for Susanne, her douyter, with Joachym, hir hosebonde, and with alle hir kynesmen, for a foul thing was not foundun in hir.
1.64: Forsothe Danyel was maad greet in the siyt of the puple, fro that dai and afterward.

1.1: Forsothe Danyel eet with the kyng, and was onourid aboue alle the frendis of hym.
1.2: Also an idol, Bel bi name, was at Babiloyne, and twelue mesuris of cleene flour, of whiche mesuris eche conteynede thre buyschels, and fourti scheep, and sixe mesuris of wyn, that ben clepid amfris, weren spendid in it ech day.
1.4: And the kyng worschipede that Beel, and yede ech dai to onoure hym; certis Danyel worschipide his God. And the kyng seide to hym, Whi worschipist thou not Beel?
1.5: Which answeride, and seide to him, For Y worschipe not idols maad bi hond, but God lyuynge, that made of nouyt heuene and erthe, and hath power of ech fleisch.
1.6: And the kyng seide to hym, Whether it semeth not to thee, that Bel is a lyuynge god? whether thou seest not, hou grete thingis he etith and drynkith ech dai?
1.7: And Daniel seide leiyinge, Kyng, erre thou not; for whi this Bel is of clei with ynne, and of bras withoutforth, and etith not ony tyme.
1.8: And the king was wroth, and clepide the preestis therof, and seide to hem, If ye seien not to me, who it is that etith these costis, ye schulen die.
1.9: Forsothe if ye schewen that Bel etith these thingis, Daniel schal die, for he blasfemede Bel. And Daniel seide to the king, Be it don bi thi word.
1.10: Forsothe the prestis of Bel weren seuenti, outakun wyues, and litle children, ether seruauntis, and sones. And the kyng cam with Daniel in to the temple of Bel.
1.11: And the preestis of Bel seiden, Lo! we schulen go out, and thou, kyng, sette meetis, and meddle wyn, and close thou the dore, and aseele it with thi ryng.
1.12: And whanne thou entrist eerli, if thou fyndist not alle thingis etun of Bel, we schulen die bi deth, ether Daniel schal die, that liede ayens vs.
1.13: Sotheli thei tristiden, for thei hadden maad a priuy entryng vndur the boord, and bi it thei entriden euere, and deuouriden tho thingis.
1.14: Forsothe it was don, aftir that thei yeden out, and the king settide metis bifor Bel, Daniel comaundide to hise children, and thei brouyten aischis, and he riddlide thorouy al the temple bifor the kyng. And thei yeden out, and closiden the dore, and aseeliden with the ryng of the kyng, and yeden forth.
1.15: But the preestis entriden in niyt, bi her custom, and the wyues, and children of hem, and eeten and drunken alle thingis.
1.16: Forsothe the kyng roos moost eerli, and Daniel with hym.
1.17: And the kyng seide, Daniel, whether the seelis ben saaf? And he answeride, King, tho ben saaf.
1.18: And anoon whanne thei hadden openyd the dore, the king biheelde the boord, and he criede an hiy with a greet vois, Bel, thou art greet, and no gile is at thee.
1.19: And Daniel leiyede, and he helde the kyng, that he entride not with ynne. And Daniel seide, Lo! the pawment, perseyue thou whos steppis these ben.
1.20: And the kyng seide, Y se steppis of men, and of wymmen, and of yonge children. And the kyng was wrooth.
1.21: Thanne the kyng took the preestis, and the wyues, and children of hem; and thei schewiden to hym litle priuy doris, bi whiche thei entriden, and wastiden tho thingis that weren on the boord.
1.22: Therfor the kyng killide hem, and bitook Bel in to the power of Daniel, which distriede thilke Bel, and his temple.
1.23: And a greet dragoun was in that place, and Babiloyns worschipiden it.
1.24: And the kyng seide to Daniel, Lo! now thou maist not seie, that this is not a quik god; therfor worschipe thou hym.
1.25: And Daniel seide to the kyng, Y worschipe my Lord God, for he is God lyuynge.
1.26: But thou, kyng, yyue power to me, and Y schal sle the dragoun, with out swerd and staf. And the kyng seide, Y yyue to thee.
1.27: Therfor Daniel took pitch, and talow, and heeris, and sethide togidere; and he made gobetis, and yaf in to the mouth of the dragun; and the dragun was al to-brokun. And Daniel seide, Lo! whom ye worschipiden.
1.28: And whanne Babiloynes hadden herd this thing, thei hadden indignacioun greetli; and thei weren gaderid ayens the king, and seiden, The king is maad a Jew; he distriede Bel, and killide the dragun, and slow the preestis.
1.29: And thei seiden, whanne thei weren comun to the kyng, Bitake thou to vs Daniel, that distriede Bel, and killide the dragun; ellis we schulen sle thee, and thin hous.
1.30: Therfor the kyng siy, that thei fellen in on hym greetli; and he was compellid bi nede, and he bitook Daniel to hem.
1.31: Whiche senten hym in to the lake of liouns, and he was there seuene daies.
1.32: Certis seuene liouns weren in the lake, and twei bodies and twei scheep weren youun to hem ech dai. And thanne tho weren not youun to hem, that thei schulden deuoure Daniel.
1.33: Forsothe Abacuk, the profete, was in Judee, and he hadde soden potage, and hadde set in looues in a litil panyere; and he yede in to the feeld, to bere to reperis.
1.34: And the aungel of the Lord seide to Abacuk, Bere thou the mete, which thou hast, in to Babiloyne, to Daniel, which is in the lake of liouns.
1.35: And Abacuk seide, Lord, Y siy not Babiloyne, and Y knew not the lake.
1.36: And the aungel of the Lord took hym bi his top, and bar hym bi the heer of his heed; and he `settide thilke Abacuk in Babiloyne, on the lake, in the fersnesse of his spirit.
1.37: And Abacuk criede, and seide, Daniel, the seruaunt of God, take thou the mete, that God hath sent to thee.
1.38: And Daniel seide, Lord God, thou hast mynde on me, and hast not forsake hem that louen thee.
1.39: And Daniel roos, and eet; certis the aungel of the Lord restoride Abacuk anoon in his place.
1.40: Therfor the kyng cam in the seuenthe dai to biweile Danyel; and he cam to the lake, and lokide in, and lo! Daniel sittynge in the myddis of liouns.
1.41: The kyng criede an hiy with greet vois, and seide, Lord God of Daniel, thou art greet; and the kyng drow hym out of the lake.
1.42: Certis he sente in to the lake hem, that weren cause of his perdicioun, and thei weren deuourid in a moment bifor him.

1.1: And it was don, aftir that Alisaundre of Filip, king of Macedoyne, which regnede first in Grece, and yede out of the lond of Sethym, smoot Darius, king of Perseis and of Medeis,
1.2: he ordeynede many batels, and gat strengthis of alle; and he slow the kingis of erthe,
1.3: and passide forth til to endis of erthe, and took spuylis of multitude of folkis; and the erthe was stille in siyt of hym. And he gaderide vertu, and oost ful strong, and the herte of hym was enhaunsid and lift vp.
1.4: And he gat the cuntreis of folkis, and tirauntis; and thei weren maad to hym in to tribut.
1.5: And after these thingis he felle in to bed, and knew that he schulde die.
1.6: And he clepide his noble children, that weren nurschid with hym fro yongthe, and departide to hem his kingdom, whanne he lyuede yit.
1.7: And Alisaundre regnede twelue yeer, and was deed.
1.8: And his children weldiden the rewme,
1.9: ech in his place, and alle puttiden to hem diademys aftir his deth, and the sones of hem after hem, many yeeris; and yuels weren multiplied in erthe.
1.10: And ther wente out of hem a roote of synne, Antiok the noble, the sone of Antiok kyng, that was at Rome in ostage, and regnede in the hundrid and seuene and thrittithe yeer of the rewme of Grekis.
1.11: In tho daies wickid sones `of Israel wenten out, and counseiliden many, and seide, Go we, and ordeyne we testament with hethene men, that ben aboute vs; for sithen we departiden fro hem, many yuels foundun vs.
1.12: And the word was seyn good bifore the iyen of hem.
1.13: And summe of the puple senten, and wenten to the kyng; and he yaf power to hem for to do riytwisnesse of hethene men.
1.14: And thei bildiden a scole in Jerusalem, bi lawis of naciouns;
1.15: and maden to hem prepucies, and wenten awei fro the hooli testament, and weren ioyned to naciouns, and weren seeld for to do yuel.
1.16: And the rewme hadde prosperite in the siyt of Antiok, and he bigan for to regne in the lond of Egipt, that he schulde regne on twei rewmes.
1.17: And he entride in to Egipt with a greuouse multitude, in charis, and olifauntis, and horse men, `ether kniytis, and plenteuouse multitude of schippis,
1.18: and he ordeynede batel ayens Tholome, kyng of Egipt; and Tolome dredde of his face, and flei; and many weren woundid, and fellen doun.
1.19: And he took the stronge citees in the lond of Egipt, and took the preies of the lond of Egipt.
1.20: And Antiok turnede, after that he smoot Egipt, in the hundrid and thre and fourtithe yeer, and stiede to Israel. And he stiede to Jerusalem with a greuouse multitude,
1.21: and entride in to the halewyng with pride; and he took the goldun auter, and the candilstike of liyt, and alle vessels therof, and the boord of proposicioun, and vessels of fletynge sacrifices, and cruetis, and goldun morteris, and veil, and crownes, and goldun ournement that was in the face of the temple; and he brak alle.
1.23: And he took siluer and gold, and alle desirable vessels, and he took the priuy tresours, whiche he foond; and whanne he hadde takun vp alle thingis, he wente in to his lond.
1.24: And he made slauyter of men, and spak in greet pride.
1.25: And greet weilyng was maad in Israel, and in ech place of hem;
1.26: and princes sorewiden inwardli, and eldere men, and maidens, and yonge men weren maad sike, and fairnesse of wymmen was chaungid.
1.27: Ech hosebonde took weilyng, and thei that saten in hosebondis bed, morenyden.
1.28: And the lond was mouyd togidere on men dwellynge therynne, and al the hous of Jacob was clothid with confusioun.
1.29: And aftir twei yeeris of daies, the kyng sente a prince of tributis in to the citees of Juda, and he cam to Jerusalem with greet cumpanye.
1.30: And he spak to hem pesible wordis in gile, and thei bileuyden to hym. And sudeynli he felle in on the citee, and smoot it with a greet wounde, and loste myche puple of Israel.
1.31: And he took preies of the citee, and brente it with fier, and distriede housis therof, and wallis therof in cumpas.
1.32: And thei ledden wymmen caitif, and children, and weldiden beestis.
1.33: And thei bildiden the citee of Dauid with greet wal and sad, and sadde touris; and it was maad to hem in to an hiy tour.
1.34: And thei puttiden there a folc of synneris, wickid men, and thei weren strong in it; and thei puttiden armeris, and metis, and gaderiden preies of Jerusalem;
1.35: and puttiden vp there, and weren maad in to a greet snare.
1.36: And this thing was maad to aspiyngis in yuel, `ether tresouns, to halewyng, and in to an yuel deuel in Israel euere more.
1.37: And thei schedden out innocent blood, bi cumpas of the halewyng, and defouliden the halewyng.
1.38: And dwelleris of Jerusalem fledden for hem, and it was maad abitacioun of straungeris, and it was maad straunge to his seed, and sones therof forsoken it.
1.39: The halewyng therof was desolat as wildirnesse; feeste daies therof weren turned in to mourenyng, sabotis therof in to schenschip, onouris therof in to nouyt.
1.40: Bi the glorie therof the yuel fame therof was multiplied, and hyynesse therof was turned in to mournyng.
1.41: And kyng Antiok wroot to al his rewme, that al the puple schulde be oon. And thei forsoken ech man his lawe;
1.42: and alle folkis consentiden bi the word of kyng Antiok,
1.43: and many of Israel consentiden to him, and sacrifieden to idols, and defouliden sabot.
1.44: And king Antiok sente bokis bi the hondis of messangeris in to Jerusalem, and in to alle citees of Judee, that thei schulden sue lawis of folkis of erthe,
1.45: and schulden forbede brent sacrifices, and sacrifices, and plesyngis for to be don in the temple of God, and that thei schulden forbede the sabot for to be halewid, and solempne daies,
1.46: and hooli thingis for to be defoulid, and the hooli puple of Israel.
1.47: And he comaundide auteris for to be bildid, and templis, and idols; and swynes fleisch for to be sacrifisid, and vncleene beestis;
